items.title: Greeicy Reflects on Her Karol G Friendship, First Billboard No. 1 Hit & More: ‘This Is My Best Year’
items.summary:
Greeicy has forged a music and acting career since the age of 15. In 2018, she was a Billboard Latin on the Rise artist and the following year she nabbed a best new artist nomination at the Latin Grammys. However, “among the many lovely things that happened to me this year,” she says 2026 has been the most defining of her career. 

“I love it, because for me, it’s impossible not to feel that this is my best year—to feel that wonderful things have happened to me—but I also love the thought that what is happening to me today is the result of the work put in over the years. This didn’t happen overnight,” the Colombian artist said in the latest episode of Billboard’s “Cafecito Con” video series. 

This year, Greeicy achieved her first-ever No. 1 on a Billboard chart when “Yapaque,” her collaboration with Farruko and Steve Aoki, reached the top of the Latin Airplay in July. In the summer, she formed part of Karol G’s Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour on select dates, where they performed their collaboration “Amiga Mía” live for the first time. And earlier this month, her album Candela was nominated for best contemporary tropical album at the Latin Grammys. 

“I think I’ve come to an understanding this year—it’s not that I’m not a dreamer, but because I grew up in an environment that was economically limited in many ways, I ended up limiting my own dreams, too. I used to say, ‘How wonderful it would be to be a singer,’ but I saw it more as a game than as a real possibility,” she shared. “This year, looking at the reality I’m living—a life I never even imagined for myself—I…
items.t: Greeicy Reflects on Her Karol G Friendship, First Billboard No. 1 Hit & More: ‘This Is My Best Year’

items.title: The New James Bond Has Been Cast. Who Will Do the Next Theme Song?
items.summary:
It’s over. The psychodrama that has enveloped the casting of the next James Bond reached its conclusion on Monday (Nov. 16) when Robert Pattinson assumed the role of 007 . 

The announcement came after a five-year search which reportedly included potentials such as Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult. Go back even further, and Idris Elba and Henry Cavill have been linked with the role since Daniel Craig announced that No Time to Die (2021) would be his final outing in the role. If you were a British actor and 6’0 or above you were bound to be given some consideration for this role. (Tough luck, Tom Holland.)

Related 

007 on the Hot 100: James Bond Songs From Lowest to Highest Charting 

Pattison will be joined by Denis Villeneuve, director of the Dune trilogy (the upcoming Dune 3 flick will star Pattison) and Arrival . He joins as the Bond franchise enters a new era, with Amazon MGM taking control of the beloved series for its 26th official outing, after decades under the stewardship of the Broccoli family and producer Michael Wilson.

Now comes the fun part: the Bond song. Nearly all of the movies has been soundtracked with a signature, original song for its opening credit sequence, a tradition that began with Shirley Bassey ’s iconic “Goldfinger” from 1964. 

Music’s finest has since tackled the mission with chart success , to boot. Duran Duran ’s “A View to Kill” is the only Bond song to hit No. 1 on Billboard’s Hot 100 , with Carly Simon (1977’s “Nobody Does it Better,” No. 2), Paul McCartney (1973’s “Live and Let Die,” No. 2) and Sheena Easton (1981’s “For…
items.t: The New James Bond Has Been Cast. Who Will Do the Next Theme Song?

Sticky M.A. came out first to perform “To pue’ ser.” Tangana joined him for “Explícame,” kicking off a stripped-down set during which songs rolled one into the next with barely a pause — and hardly a word in between.

items.title: The Longest-Leading Billboard Hot 100 No. 1s: ‘Choosin’ Texas’ & More
items.summary:
Beginning with Debby Boone’s “You Light Up My Life” in 1977, a relatively select few smashes have led the Billboard Hot 100 for at least 10 weeks. How few? Just a mere 4% of all Hot 100 No. 1s dating to the chart’s launch on Aug. 4, 1958, have earned the achievement.

Olivia Newton-John’s “Physical” flexed 10 weeks at No. 1 in 1981-82, and that smash and Boone’s shared the mark for the longest Hot 100 reign for more than a decade, until Boyz II Men’s “End of the Road” dominated for 13 weeks in 1992. That best lasted briefly, as Whitney Houston’s “I Will Always Love You” led for 14 weeks in late 1992/early 1993. In 1995-96, Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men’s “One Sweet Day” ran up 16 weeks at No. 1, a milestone that held for more than 23 years. (Songs began logging longer No. 1 stays after the Hot 100 adopted electronically tracked data, according to Luminate, in late 1991.)

In 2017, Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee’s “Despacito,” featuring Justin Bieber, tied the No. 1 run of “One Sweet Day.” By 2019, Lil Nas X’s “Old Town Road,” featuring Billy Ray Cyrus, collected 19 weeks atop the Hot 100, a mark matched by Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy)” beginning in July 2024.

Related 

Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Holds for Record-Extending 28th Week Atop Hot 100 

On the Sept. 5, 2026-dated Hot 100, Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” became the sole longest-leading non-holiday hit, with its 20th week at No. 1. As of the Nov. 21 survey, it’s the overall record holder with 28 weeks, having surpassed Mariah Carey’s “All I Want for Christmas Is You,” which has jingled to No. 1 for 22 weeks…
items.t: The Longest-Leading Billboard Hot 100 No. 1s: ‘Choosin’ Texas’ & More

items.title: Columbia Leads, Indies Shine, Island Extends BNA Streak: Big 4 Grammy Categories by Record Label
items.summary:
Columbia Records emerged Monday (Nov. 16) with nine nominations among the traditional Big Four Grammy categories of album, record and song of the year and best new artist for the 2027 ceremony, easily leading all record labels among those areas of the general field. That’s the most nominations in the Big Four since Interscope had 13 for the 2024 ceremony.

Ella Langley led the way for Columbia, with nominations in each of the Big Four — making her the fifth artist since the expansion of the categories to land nominations in each of the major general field areas, joining Sabrina Carpenter (2025), Chappell Roan (2025), Olivia Rodrigo (2022) and Billie Eilish (2020). (Eilish famously swept them all, only the second time that has ever happened, after Christopher Cross in 1981.) Langley’s “Choosin Texas” shattered the record for most weeks at No. 1 on the Hot 100 this year, at 28 weeks and counting, while her album Dandelion reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200 in April. Joining Langley among Columbia’s nominees is Rosalía , whose LUX album and single “Berghain” were nominated for album, record and song (she got a BNA nom herself in 2020), while Tame Impala and JENNIE ’s “Dracula” (record) and Slayyyter , signed to RECORDS/Columbia (BNA) rounded out the label’s Big Four nominees.

items.title: Don Toliver & Cardi B Dominate Nominations: Rap Grammy Reactions
items.summary:
The 2027 Grammy nominations are here and there are some interesting subplots in the Rap category, so I’m here to break some of them down for you.

The main story is that rap was shut out of album of the year, song of the year and record of the year. Now, depending on you ask, that could be a bad, the sky is falling sort of omen, or it could be that some may feel like the Grammys are a bit out of touch when it comes to rap music. I think, in this case, two things can be true. There’s also the fact that Drake didn’t submit anything from his triple-release of Iceman , Maid of Honour and Habibti for consideration, as the Toronto rapper seems to be unimpressed with the Grammys as an institution, clique and a label these days.

Something that the Grammys did get right, though, is rewarding Don Toliver for his 2026. His Octane album has been a mainstay on the charts and is arguably the consensus rap album of year — a status it’s basically held since it dropped in January. We gotta also acknowledge Cardi B, who after making fans wait seven years for her to follow up her debut Invasion of Privacy , has four nominations to her name this year. She and Don have been rap’s dominant mainstream acts this year, alongside Yung Miami with her breakout hit “Spend Dat” — which, for my money, is the rap song of year.

Then we have a respected rap veteran in Wale, and some legends with Busta Rhymes, T.I. and De La Soul.

Amazon took over the franchise last February and in May, they confirmed that the search for the next 007 was officially underway.

items.title: Justice’s ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ score will be the only video game soundtrack the band ever do
items.summary:
Justice have said that their score for Grand Theft Auto 6 will be the only video game soundtrack they ever do.

READ MORE: Every song confirmed for the ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ soundtrack so far 

Last month, Rockstar Games confirmed that dance titans Justice had composed an original score for Grand Theft Auto 6 . So far, two songs from the project have been released –  ‘Flower In A Hurricane’, which features Tame Impala , SZA and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard , and Gesaffelstein collab ‘Pusher’.

The fifty-track, three hour collection will be available to stream December 11 and the record will also be getting a physical release, with a range of vinyl available to pre-order now.

Before that, fans will be able to hear Justice’s music later this week (November 19) when Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases.

In a new interview with French publication Rockyrama , Justice’s Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay have spoken about their decision to work on the highly-anticipated video game.

“When [the offer] arrived on the table, we thought : “If there’s one video game we have to do, it’s this one.” As soon as we accepted and started working [on it], we thought it would probably be the first and last score we’ll ever do for a video game,” they said.

According to the band, Rockstar weren’t looking for a specific type of sound or music style for the Grand Theft Auto 6 score. “but rather the emotion that the music should give the player at specific moments.”

They went on to call their Grand Theft Auto 6 score a “special project” but confirmed that they consider it a “real” Justice…
items.t: Justice’s ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ score will be the only video game soundtrack the band ever do

items.title: Johnny Depp’s Hollywood return ‘Ebenezer’ hits top of box office
items.summary:
Johnny Depp ’s Ebenezer is a box office hit despite middling reviews from critics.

Director Ti West’s new take on Charles Dickens’ classic novella A Christmas Carol sees Depp take on the role of Ebenezer Scrooge with Ian McKellen, Rupert Grint and Daisy Ridley also starring.

Ebenezer hit cinemas on Friday (November 13) and across its opening weekend, took a reported $42million worldwide, making it the number one film at the box office. It was the most popular film in UK cinemas, taking $5.4million. Ebenezer also topped the box office in Italy, Mexico, Spain, Poland, Belgium and Central America (via Variety ).

Ahead of its release, Ebenezer received middling reviews from critics and currently has a Rotten Tomatoes score of just 54 per cent. However the response from movie goers has been a lot more positive with Ebenezer racking up a 90 per cent score on the review aggregate site’s fan-voted ‘Popcornmeter’.

Ebenezer is also Johnny Depp’s first major studio movie since 2018’s Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes Of Grindelwald. The same year the Harry Potter prequel was released, Depp’s ex-wife Amber Heard wrote an op-ed for The Washington Post in which she alleged she was domestically abused by the actor

items.title: Peter Hook tells Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame why New Order will never get back together (without Oasis reunion money)

The bassist attended the Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame ceremony on Saturday (November 14) as Joy Division and New Order were inducted together. He appeared at the event without any of the other bandmates present, and performed ‘Love Will Tear Us Apart’ and ‘Bizarre Love Triangle’ alongside Deftones and Chvrches .

Stephen Morris and Gillian Gilbert both did not attend due to health reasons, with Gilbert battling cancer.   Bernard Sumner did not show up on the night either.

Hook played with Joy Division until they became New Order when Ian Curtis took his own life in 1980, before parting ways with the band in 2007 – leading to years of legal battle and trading barbs. items.title: ‘I have to sell my bum on OnlyFans to go on tour’: Kate Nash on fame, feminism and fighting the music business
items.summary:
She threw a (metaphorical) brick through Spotify’s window and exposed industry failings with her ‘Butts for Tour Buses’ campaign. Now the singer is embracing her Irish roots with her new album’s fighting spirit

Kate Nash was standing on a fire truck in a showgirl outfit complete with white tights and pink G-string, shouting through a loudhailer about the music industry’s failure to pay artists fairly, when she wondered if she’d gone too far. It was 2024 and the truck, which made pit stops outside the London offices of Spotify and Live Nation, had a large black-and-white picture of Nash’s bum on the back along with the words “Butts for Tour Buses” – a reference to her newly launched OnlyFans account, which she was using to fund her tour.

That afternoon, she called her manager Kat. “I told her: ‘I’ve thrown a brick through the window at Spotify.’ She went: ‘What, literally?’ and I said: ‘No, but I’ve been standing outside their offices with a megaphone, so that relationship is over. I don’t think we’ll be making their New Music Friday feature.’ And we didn’t.” [see footnote]

items.title: ‘A songbook for protest movements’: how did this secret mission to smuggle antifascist music out of Spain ever get forgotten?
items.summary:
In 1961, a group of Italian creatives crossed the border to collect anti-Franco resistance songs and share them with the world – sparking intense backlash from the dictator. A new documentary retraces that perilous journey

In the summer of 1961, four Italians crossed the Pyrenees into fascist Spain. Unknown to the border guards, their car was loaded with microfilm, a tape recorder and, tucked in the pocket of a writer and musician named Sergio Liberovici, a book of matches – each split in half, etched with the addresses of Spanish antifascists in miniature and glued back together, a hairline fracture concealing secrets that, if discovered, could result in jail or worse.

Along with Michele Luciano Straniero, Emilio Jona and Margherita Galante Garrone, Liberovici was a member of a leftwing collective named Cantacronache. Formed in 1958 and counting Italo Calvino and Umberto Eco among their collaborators, the collective was repulsed by the superficiality of Italian pop music and hoped to revitalise culture with Brechtian realism. At the time, Italy was fiercely divided into leftwing and rightwing political camps, and it was a record label, Italia Canta, linked to the Italian Communist party, that financed the trip. Its goal: to secretly document the resistance songs of the anti-Franco underground. It was a perilous task for all involved, but especially so for Cantacronache’s contacts.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘A songbook for protest movements’: how did this secret mission to smuggle antifascist music out of Spain ever get forgotten?

items.title: Ocean Colour Scene review – no other band of their era can do it like this
items.summary:
Ulster Hall, Belfast
With two sets of fathers and sons now in the group, as they play all of Moseley Shoals on its 30th anniversary, the indie stalwarts have aged into seismic and soulful performers

‘It’s only 30 years ago,” Simon Fowler says of Moseley Shoals. He would seem to mean it, but 30 years makes Ocean Colour Scene’s breakthrough album as old now as Revolver was when they were making it. The band once derided for raiding the 60s are now heritage themselves. They open the album’s anniversary tour on the stage where Led Zeppelin first played Stairway to Heaven, and you can’t help but appreciate the lineage.

They walk on to Green Onions, fresh from the Crown Bar, and open with You’ve Got It Bad, all supreme Motown stomp. Fowler sings with a hand in his pocket and looks taken aback by the welcome. The casualness is a conduit: his voice has aged into something close to peak Joe Cocker, grained at the edges, honey underneath. Lining Your Pockets is more resounding than ever.

items.title: Paris Paloma review – arena-scale alt-pop drama from a singer on her way to bigger things
items.summary:
Bristol Beacon
The UK artist combines feminist fury with accessible melodies and a dramatic flair that sees her alternately pogoing and seeking out the wind machines at the prow of the stage

People are dancing to a song they don’t know, with flower garlands in their hair and their arms around their friends. This reaction to Fairy Dance, an unreleased track written about the community that has sprung up around her music, says a lot about the moment Paris Paloma finds herself in, and tonight’s show feels for all the world like a stepping stone to bigger things.

Throughout, Paloma leans in to the built-in drama of songs from her second album, The Fatal Flaw, which pairs ornate folk arrangements with the sort of arena-sized alt-pop production favoured by Florence + the Machine. With a sculpture inspired by surrealist Ithell Colquhoun’s Tree of Veins dominating the stage, she falls to her knees to deliver high notes and seeks out wind machines at the prow of the stage, her flowing crimson dress buffeted as if on a wintry moor.

items.title: Philippines’ Carmelle wins first Eurovision contest in Asia
items.summary:
Filipino entry, pop and rap song Sobra-Sobra, takes 19-year-old to victory at grand final in Bangkok

Carmelle Collado has won the first Eurovision song contest Asia, taking the Philippines’ entry, Sobra-Sobra, to victory in Bangkok on Saturday night, at the first regional edition of the contest to be staged outside Europe.

Eleven countries competed at the One Bangkok Forum in central Bangkok, and the show ran for two and a half hours including advertising.
